title: introduce cost-simulate dry-run CLI and tenant prefill guidance exporter
author: Luca Sandoval
description:
Motivation: Operators and SREs need a safe way to preview tenant-level cost/latency tradeoffs before applying batching, prefill, and quantization defaults. This PR implements an interactive dry-run CLI 'cost-simulate' and a small exporter that emits tenant guidance playbooks (YAML) to be consumed by the defaults compiler. The tool runs the existing simulation engine over sampled tenant traffic, applies candidate batching/caching/quant profiles, and produces an evidence-backed recommendation plus a visualizable heatmap for prefill behavior.

What this PR contains: added a user-facing CLI (cmd/cost-simulate) with modes: --dry-run (local report), --export-playbook (writes YAML to stdout/file), --preview-html (generate a static HTML visualizer). Integrated the simulator with the runtime's sampling pipeline so it can re-use tenant replay traces without contacting production endpoints. Introduced a telemetry adapter to surface simulation traces and cost curves into the observability pipeline (tagged as sim.*), and a small console asset for tenant prefill heatmaps.

Important design notes: the CLI performs no writes to production; all simulations run against sampled sanitized traces. We added sanitization hooks to strip potential user PII and ensured the telemetry adapter masks identifiers. The exporter outputs pinned suggestions in the format expected by the defaults compiler: tenant_id, suggested_batch_size, suggested_prefill_policy, quant_profile_hint, expected_cost_delta_pct, confidence_score.

Testing and validation: unit tests for the simulator adapters and exporter, integration test that runs the CLI against synthetic tenant sample (included in testdata/), and an end-to-end smoke test that validates the defaults compiler accepts the exported YAML. CI initially hit a flaky scheduler test which was fixed by adding a deterministic seed in the simulator.

Migration and rollout: this is additive. Operators can install the CLI in the management workstation or run it in a sandbox job. To adopt suggestions in production, teams must review the exported YAML using existing defaults-as-code review flows. We also added a small docs page describing recommended safety thresholds and how to run a canary.

Notes: the telemetry adapter is opt-in (disabled by default) and requires a feature flag redwood.sim.telemetry=true to enable in staging. The visualizer is static and safe for sharing with customers after sanitization.

Related: ENG-4312 (simulate-based defaults), PM-2840 (tenant cost playbooks).

release_notes: Add cost-simulate CLI for safe tenant-level cost/latency dry-runs, playbook exporter for defaults-as-code, telemetry adapter (opt-in), and static prefill visualizer. Operators can dry-run and export vetted suggestions to the defaults compiler.
notes_for_ops: Telemetry disabled by default. To enable sim telemetry set redwood.sim.telemetry=true in staging. Exported playbooks must be reviewed before applying. The CLI uses sampled traces under sandbox/testdata by default. See docs/cost-simulate.md for permissions and safe-run checklist.
